newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST-Polish April yr/yr CPI seen below 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Polish April yr/yr CPI seen below 15 pct.

text.p: Polish inflation has been slowing faster than envisaged in the budget and may dip to about 15 percent this month, said Tadeusz Chroscicki, chief analyst at the government's Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS).

"The pace of the reduction in price growth is faster than assumed in the budget and already in April the year-on-year inflation may not exceed 15 percent," Chroscicki said in his macroeconomic forecast submitted monthly to Reuters.
He said industrial output growth remained strong throughout the first quarter with manufacturing output in the first half of 1997 likely to be 12 percent higher than a year ago.
This would be accompanied by a relative stabilisation of capital and energy-intensive mining and utilities sectors.
He said construction output was exceptionally strong, recording a 24 percent increase over the first quarter of 1996 with a significant improvement in housing construction.

Chroscicki added, however, the widening trade deficit remained a serious threat for the stability of the economy and the deficit could rise in the first half to $5.6 billion, 1.8-times more than last year's gap.

NOTES: Official forex reserves are hard currencies held by the central bank while net reserves are the total amount of foreign exchange in the banking system. Indicators marked (F) are forecasts. * Counted from start of year.
